text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Armed gangsters stage a daring raid in Nairobi, loot and ransack a main street's business premises and offices.
- President Daniel arap Moi says Kenya government will pay for electricity from Uganda at current market rates.
- Vice-President Professor George Saitoti says AIDS-related deaths will top more than a million in three years.
- Fallen Kenya Finance Bank faces liquidation if the appointed depositors' committee fails to work out strategies to re-open it by October 31 1996.

- 63 coffee farmers from Kiambu and Thika districts oppose plans by the Kenya Planters Cooperative Union (KPCU) to borrow an additional 3 billion shillings saying the Union has no mandate to borrow money without full approval from the farmers.

- President Daniel arap Moi declares he is as "fit as a fiddle" to run for another term of office and tells Kenyans to disregard any rumours that he is not in a position to defend his seat in the next general election.

- This week's sacking of John Sambu as Minister for Environment and Natural Resources to replace him with Henry Kosgey is part of President Moi's pre-election strategy to woo back populous Nandi tribe into the ruling party mainstream.
